shortDescription: Ireland's manufacturing sector expanded robustly again in August and at close to a four-year high as new orders rose at the sharpest pace since April 2022, a business survey showed on Tuesday.

children: Ireland's manufacturing sector expanded robustly again in August and at close to a four-year high as new orders rose at the sharpest pace since April 2022, a business survey showed on Tuesday.
The AIB Ireland Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index, compiled by S&P Global, rose to 55.4 in August from 55.1 in July. The 50 mark separates growth from contraction.
Manufacturing activity has not contracted since December 2024, and growth has accelerated over the past five months at the fastest rate since that run began.
While new orders hit a 4-1/2-year high, new business from abroad increased at a much weaker pace for the second successive month due to uncertainty caused by the war in the Middle East.
The conflict also contributed to continued supply-chain delays, with the sharp rate of deterioration in suppliers' delivery times only slightly softer than in July.
Delays receiving purchased items caused a further build-up in backlogs of work, the fifth in the past six months.
The rate of input price inflation ticked up month-on-month, well below the near-four-year peak reached in May but still much higher than the levels prior to the conflict.
Manufacturers also continued to pass those costs on to their customers. The pace of price increases, while still sharp, slowed to a five-month low.
